newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican peso reverses weakness on foreign buyers.
newsitem.headline: Mexican peso reverses weakness on foreign buyers.

text.p: The Mexican peso reversed early weakness to close slightly firmer against the dollar after domestic and foreign buyers stepped into the local markets ahead of the upcoming long weekend.
"Several banks took advantage of a stronger dollar to acquire peso investments at attractive prices," a peso trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso closed 0.85 of a centavo firmer at 7.5430/7.5465 per dollar, while 24-hour contracts were 0.90 of a centavo firmer at 7.5410/7.5440 per dollar.

Traders said that the peso weakened against the dollar earlier due to speculative trade following the sharp fall in Cetes rates at Tuesday night's primary auction and yields on the U.S. 30-year Treasury bond rebounding to 7.15 percent.

"People this morning were speculating on the fall in Cetes rates and increases in the U.S. long bond rate...but had to dump long dollar positions when the peso failed to stay weaker than 7.57 per dollar," a trader said.
The benchmark spot peso reached 7.5650/7.5710 per dollar at its weakest on Wednesday.
The same-day peso closed earlier 1.70 centavos weaker at 7.5465/7.5500 per dollar.
Traders were expecting swaps all day on Thursday, as 48-hour contracts will not have to be settled until after the Independence Day holiday on Monday.
